findings.finding: The original helper selects the exact original target and its nearest vertically scrollable ancestor, then returns null when that ancestor has no positive viewport interval. That occurs before any wheel; waitRead repeats the same failing geometry. The actual model selector uses a constrained-height overflow-y-auto grid, so nested scroll owners are real source structure. This establishes the described source-level dead branch; it does not establish exclusive causation for any historical Resume receipt, which did not retain every ancestor rectangle/count.

The proposal retains selector/text/one-match admission, original target rectangle, nearest-ancestor lookup and zero-size refusal. The positive nearest-viewport branch must retain the complete old return path, including optional target-center hit behavior and its absence by default. The fallback is confined to bottom<=top and cannot return target visible:true.

Candidates come only from the target's actual ancestor chain above the unavailable inner scrollport and use the existing vertical overflow predicate. No named dialog, unrelated container, global fallback, alternate point or probe wheel is authorized. A candidate needs finite positive exposed area after viewport and per-axis clipping intersections; intervening fixed clips cannot be treated as removable by an outer vertical wheel.

The chosen single center point must actually hit that candidate or a descendant whose nearest vertical scroll owner is exactly the candidate. A foreign overlay, different nested owner, absent hit or exhausted range in the intended direction refuses. Direction follows the original nested scrollport being exposed, not offscreen/clipped target-content center. When multiple nested scrollports are offscreen, the chosen outer operation must expose the relevant intervening scrollport before the next unchanged loop can progress inward. These are necessary constraints already in the R1, not a newly authored implementation.

The existing tests import createDesktopUiControls and run the actual generated expression in runInNewContext. They assert one default disabled-control read with no hit calls or input; the opt-in case asserts exactly two original center-hit coordinates and the exact one centering wheel with delta -276. They also require the identical expression on each loop read. These exact old cases would expose a broad rewrite of the positive-viewport path and must remain unchanged.

The selected appended cases can use the existing real-expression VM seam and recorded CDP commands. Geometry changes only in response to the matching recorded wheel; outer then inner progress and the above-viewport direction case cannot be satisfied by faking a helper return. Fully clipped/overlay/foreign-owner and missing/duplicate-target cases require zero wheel. The existing fake-Date API supports bounded timeout refusal without a real 30-second wait. No new test framework, native process or separate CI round is needed or selected.
